prompt_text: Who is the best dentist in Dallas for a dental implant?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” dentist — the right provider depends on your needs (type of implant, medical history, budget, insurance, sedation needs, how comfortable you feel with the dentist). For dental implants you’ll usually want a specialist with lots of implant experience: an oral & maxillofacial surgeon, a periodontist, or a prosthodontist (often working together with your restorative dentist).

Quick guidance and next steps
- Decide what you need: single-tooth implant, multiple implants, full-arch replacement, bone graft/sinus lift, sedation/general anesthesia.
- Look for the right specialist:
  - Oral & maxillofacial surgeons: surgical placement + sedation expertise.
  - Periodontists: surgical placement with emphasis on gum/biologic health.
  - Prosthodontists: specialists in the implant crown/bridge/denture/restoration.
- Credentials & experience to check:
  - Board certification (American Board of Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery, American Board of Periodontology, American Board of Prosthodontics) or membership in AAID/Academy of Osseointegration.
  - How many implants they place per year and examples/case photos.
  - Use of CBCT (3D X-ray) and guided surgery.
  - Implant systems used (Straumann, Nobel Biocare, Zimmer, etc.) and follow-up/warranty.
- Practical checks:
  - Read recent patient reviews (Google, Yelp, Healthgrades).
  - Ask who does the crown/restoration — surgeon or restorative dentist? (Better when team coordinates.)
  - Get a written treatment plan, timeline, total cost, and financing options.
  - Ask about complications policy and follow-up care.

If you want, I can:
- Search for highly rated implant specialists in Dallas near your zip code,
- Compare several practices’ credentials, patient ratings, and services,
- Or give a list of questions to ask at a consultation.

Which would you prefer, and what part of Dallas (zip code or neighborhood) are you in? Any insurance or sedation needs?
